surfaceContracts.targetObserved: GET /api/v1/notification/list and /unread-count are owner-authenticated but expose a different schema and status filter

surfaceContracts.targetObserved: POST read/unread/mark-all/clear-all plus hard deletes; acknowledge is absent

surfaceContracts.source: subscribe, unsubscribe, and status routes backed by browser permission state

ownershipRules.rule: Every owner read or mutation derives the normalized wallet solely from the verified principal and hides foreign IDs with 404.
Admin reads and mutations use explicit operation permissions; manage does not silently grant unrelated read, delivery, or template authority.
Domain publishers use a non-browser internal service identity scoped to approved event types and recipient derivation rules.
user_id, wallet recipient, email recipient, broadcast, plan targeting, and channel cannot contradict one another.
Broadcast and plan fanout require explicit authorization, audience resolution, bounded cardinality, and auditable actor identity.

deliveryRules.rule: Persist the notification and delivery jobs atomically before any transport dispatch.
Notification read state, per-channel delivery state, provider acceptance, client acknowledgement, click state, and terminal failure are independent fields.
SMTP/provider acceptance is not user delivery; absent provider configuration must never report sent.
In-app success requires durable persistence; realtime fanout is best-effort and replayable from durable state.
Transient errors use bounded exponential backoff with jitter; permanent errors terminate without retry.
Exhausted jobs enter a queryable dead-letter state with redrive authorization and audit history.
SSE replay uses a durable monotonic cursor or Last-Event-ID policy and deduplicates reconnect delivery.
Preferences, quiet hours, legal/security exceptions, expiry, and channel eligibility are evaluated by the backend before jobs are created.

idempotencyRules.rule: Publisher requests require an idempotency key scoped to service principal and event type with a request hash.
Domain delivery is unique by source event identity, recipient, template/version, and channel.
Workers claim jobs with leases and compare-and-set transitions so crashes cannot produce uncontrolled duplicate sends.
Provider message IDs and accepted responses are recorded for deduplication and reconciliation.
Read/unread/delete/bulk operations are retry-safe and return stable affected-count semantics.

privacyRules.rule: Logs and traces never contain message bodies, template variables, email addresses, tokens, or raw provider payloads.
Template rendering is strict, size-bounded, allowlisted, and safe for text and HTML contexts.
Action and image URLs are restricted to approved schemes/origins and cannot create script or tracking injection.
Retention, expiry, user deletion, legal hold, and account erasure semantics are explicit per channel.
SMTP, push, Redis, database, and internal identity secrets come from managed secrets and are never accepted in browser payloads.

migrationRequirements: declare the canonical source and target schemas and one write authority
use additive versioned migrations rather than startup DDL
backfill wallet_notifications, read/click/delivery fields, preferences, templates, and publisher event identities
preserve normalized wallet ownership and broadcast semantics
run count, checksum, state-distribution, orphan, and duplicate reconciliation
support resumable batches with checkpoints and bounded locks
prove forward compatibility, rollback compatibility, and no destructive migration without reviewed necessity
observabilityRequirements: queue depth and oldest-job age by channel
enqueue, attempt, provider-acceptance, terminal-failure, retry, and dead-letter counters
SSE active connections, reconnects, lag, replay count, and fanout failures
preference suppressions and invalid-recipient metrics without PII labels
template render failures and version distribution
alerts and runbooks for delivery lag, error budget, dead letters, reconciliation drift, and provider outages
cutoverRequirements: shadow reads compare source and target without exposing target results
publisher canary uses explicit allowlisted event types and tenants/wallets
single-writer switch is configuration-controlled and audited
rollback preserves idempotency and does not replay already accepted provider sends
SSE clients reconnect across the switch without losing or duplicating durable events
legacy writes are disabled only after reconciliation and rollback-window approval

blockers.summary: Source and target methods, prefixes, payloads, fields, envelopes, and status codes are not locked by executable compatibility tests.
blockers.resolution: Implement an explicit adapter or versioned API and contract-test every A11 surface against the pinned source behavior.

blockers.summary: Legacy wallet_notifications and candidate notifications/templates are incompatible write models, and the candidate DDL omits columns its queries require.
blockers.resolution: Choose one schema authority, add versioned constraints and mappings, and prove clean-database plus upgraded-database behavior.

blockers.summary: The service mutates schema and seeds templates/sample user data during startup.
blockers.resolution: Move all DDL and controlled seed data to additive reviewed migrations; prohibit sample data in production startup.

blockers.summary: Direct owner authentication is present, but normalization, broadcast inclusion, foreign-resource behavior, and source owner contract parity are unproven.
blockers.resolution: Lock canonical wallet normalization and owner-scoped integration tests for every single and bulk operation.

blockers.summary: Delivery status and user read state are overloaded, and source acknowledge/click/delivery semantics are missing.
blockers.resolution: Define independent channel delivery and user engagement state machines with guarded transitions and exact affected-row checks.

blockers.summary: Owner notification preferences and quiet-hour enforcement are not implemented in the target HTTP service.
blockers.resolution: Add owner-scoped durable preferences, validation, defaults, legal exception policy, and enqueue-time enforcement.

blockers.summary: The extracted notification service has no authenticated SSE or equivalent realtime delivery route.
blockers.resolution: Implement principal-bound streaming with bounded connections, keepalive, origin policy, backpressure, and disconnect cleanup.

blockers.summary: Offline replay, broadcast replay, durable cursor, reconnect dedupe, and client acknowledgement are absent.
blockers.resolution: Define replay ordering and Last-Event-ID semantics backed by durable state and idempotent acknowledgement.

blockers.summary: Browser permission is simulated locally and push subscription/delivery lifecycle is absent.
blockers.resolution: Implement real browser permission handling, owner-scoped subscription storage, key rotation, unsubscribe, and push delivery outcomes.

blockers.summary: Admin send permits independently supplied user_id, channel, and recipient without a canonical target-resolution contract.
blockers.resolution: Validate mutually exclusive wallet/plan/broadcast targets, normalize recipients, bound fanout, and audit the verified actor.

blockers.summary: Domain publishers have no HTTP adapter or scoped internal service identity for the extracted service.
blockers.resolution: Add authenticated service-to-service publish APIs, event-type scopes, replay protection, and caller audit metadata.

blockers.summary: Producer state, notification persistence, channel jobs, and realtime fanout are not joined by an outbox/inbox transaction.
blockers.resolution: Use transactional outbox at producers, deduplicating inbox at notification service, and atomic notification+job creation.

blockers.summary: Publish, send, template mutation, and delivery jobs have no locked idempotency or deduplication keys.
blockers.resolution: Persist scoped request hashes, source event identities, job leases, provider IDs, and stable replay responses.

blockers.summary: There is no durable queue, retry classification/backoff, lease recovery, dead-letter store, or redrive workflow.
blockers.resolution: Add durable per-channel jobs, bounded retries with jitter, dead letters, authorized redrive, and crash-recovery tests.

blockers.summary: Missing SMTP configuration logs PII/content and reports success; configured SMTP performs a blocking send in an async request.
blockers.resolution: Fail closed on provider configuration, enqueue asynchronously, enforce TLS/provider policy, sanitize telemetry, and record provider outcomes.

blockers.summary: The in_app transport reports delivered without realtime fanout or client receipt.
blockers.resolution: Return durable accepted state, publish best-effort after commit, and derive delivered/acknowledged only from explicit events.

blockers.summary: Template rendering is non-strict, update responses can lose the row identity, and delete does not synchronize the in-memory registry.
blockers.resolution: Add strict typed variables, versions, preview, validation, size limits, atomic cache invalidation, and deterministic rollback.

blockers.summary: PII logging, HTML/template rendering, URL fields, retention, erasure, and secret handling lack a verified policy.
blockers.resolution: Enforce the privacy rules, sanitize content and URLs, redact telemetry, and test retention/erasure and secret boundaries.

blockers.summary: Generic tracing initialization and a bare 200 health endpoint do not prove queue, provider, database, Redis, or delivery health.
blockers.resolution: Add dependency readiness, RED metrics, queue age/depth, channel outcomes, SLOs, alerts, dashboards, and runbooks.

blockers.summary: No resumable backfill or reconciliation proves legacy history, broadcasts, preferences, templates, and delivery state in the target.
blockers.resolution: Build dry-run and resumable migration tooling with counts, checksums, distributions, duplicates, orphans, and repair reports.

blockers.summary: The notification crate is a workspace member but has no Kubernetes deployment/service, managed secrets, dependency probes, or worker topology.
blockers.resolution: Add immutable artifact deployment, service/worker separation, secrets, resource limits, startup/readiness probes, network policy, and rollback manifests.

blockers.summary: There is no declared single writer, shadow comparison, canary, reconciliation approval, or duplicate-safe rollback procedure.
blockers.resolution: Execute the locked cutover requirements with explicit go/no-go evidence and preserve the legacy path through the rollback window.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: compatibility-and-authority
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: One versioned API contract, owner/admin/internal authority matrix, and one declared write authority are approved.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: durable-schema-and-migration
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: Additive migrations, constraints, state machines, idempotency, inbox/outbox, jobs, and clean/upgrade tests pass.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: publishers-and-targeting
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: Internal service identity, HTTP adapter, source event dedupe, wallet/plan/broadcast resolution, and producer recovery tests pass.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: delivery-workers
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: Email and in-app workers prove accepted/sent/failed semantics, retry, dead-letter, redrive, provider reconciliation, and privacy controls.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: realtime-preferences-push
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: SSE replay/reconnect/ack, backend-enforced preferences/quiet hours, and real browser push lifecycle pass integration tests.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: template-admin-and-user-ux
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: Template versioning and every source user/admin interaction pass browser, accessibility, responsive, and error-state tests without sample fallback.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: backfill-observability-and-operations
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: Dry-run/backfill/reconciliation reports are clean and dependency health, metrics, alerts, dashboards, and runbooks are verified.

requiredExecutionOrder.name: shadow-canary-cutover-rollback
requiredExecutionOrder.exit: Shadow parity, canary, single-writer switch, duplicate-safe rollback rehearsal, and post-cutover reconciliation meet reviewed thresholds.

safety.readinessMeaning: Integrity validates local pinned evidence only; it does not prove runtime, delivery, migration, deployment, or production readiness.
